content_voiceover: This slide details primary induction regimens for transplant eligible newly diagnosed myeloma, combining NCCN preferred regimens with a Taiwanese reimbursement algorithm. The NCCN preferred triplet regimens are daratumumab, lenalidomide, bortezomib, and dexamethasone, or isatuximab, bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone, both category one. Other recommended options include bortezomib, lenalidomide, dexamethasone, carfilzomib based triplets, and daratumumab or isatuximab added to carfilzomib, lenalidomide, dexamethasone. The Taiwan flowchart shows treatment choice depends on insurance coverage, patient preference, comorbidities, renal function, neuropathy, hematopoietic reserve, tumor aggressiveness, and extramedullary disease. For triplets, proteasome inhibitor plus IMiD combinations like VTD or RVD are the current first line mainstay, while PI alone with VCD, or IMiD alone with CTD, are used in select circumstances. For quadruplet therapy, daratumumab VTd or daratumumab VRd are now reimbursed by Taiwan's national health insurance as of September twenty twenty five, with VTDC or PACE based regimens reserved for aggressive or refractory presentations.
keypoints: NCCN preferred triplets: daratumumab or isatuximab plus bortezomib, lenalidomide, dexamethasone, both category 1
PI plus IMiD triplets like VTD and RVD are the current first-line mainstay
PI-only (VCD) or IMiD-only (CTD) triplets are reserved for select circumstances
Quadruplet Dara-VTd or Dara-VRd gained Taiwan NHI reimbursement in September 2025
PACE-based regimens (VTD-PACE, VRD-PACE) are reserved for aggressive or high-risk disease
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, the preferred induction for transplant eligible patients is a daratumumab or isatuximab based triplet with a proteasome inhibitor, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone. PI plus IMiD combinations like VTD and RVD remain the first line mainstay. Quadruplet daratumumab regimens are increasingly standard and now reimbursed in Taiwan as of late twenty twenty five, while PACE based regimens are reserved for aggressive disease.
